question: Which of the following was the revenue collecting officer (collector general of revenue) in the Mauryan administration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Samaharta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Mauryan administration, **Samaharta** was the officer responsible for collecting revenue and taxes.
 
• The term "Samaharta" translates to "collector general of revenue," focusing on ensuring proper taxation and resource management.
 
• Samaharta oversaw the collection of various taxes, including land revenue, trade taxes, and other levies under the Mauryan empire.
 
• This position was essential for maintaining the financial stability of the Mauryan administration and supporting its vast bureaucracy and army.
 
• Revenue collected by the Samaharta contributed significantly to the empire's central treasury, managed by another officer known as the **Sannidhata**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antapala:** This term referred to officers responsible for the protection and security of the empire's frontiers.
 
• **Sannidhata:** The Sannidhata was the treasurer in the Mauryan administration, responsible for managing the empire's central treasury.
 
• **Amatya:** Amatyas were high-ranking officials who acted as ministers or advisors to the king in the Mauryan administrative hierarchy.
 
• **Revenue System:** The Mauryan empire had a well-organized revenue system, including taxes on agriculture, trade, and professions, which were crucial for sustaining the vast empire.
 
• **Arthashastra:** The administrative and economic roles of officers like Samaharta are detailed in Kautilya's Arthashastra, a seminal work on governance and economics during the Mauryan era.
